function: Ask the child to look at the letter shown and say its sound.
trigger: New beginner-level item is presented.

function: Ask the child to read the syllable shown aloud.
trigger: New letter/syllable-level item is presented.

function: Ask the child to read the word shown aloud.
trigger: New word-level item is presented.

function: Ask the child to read the paragraph aloud, at their own pace.
trigger: New paragraph-level item is presented.

function: Ask the child to read the story aloud from the beginning.
trigger: New story-level item is presented.

function: Ask a simple comprehension question about the story just read.
trigger: Child finishes reading a story-level item.

function: Ask the child to try reading the same item one more time.
trigger: The item needs a second attempt for any reason.

function: Ask the child to slow down and read at a calmer pace.
trigger: Child is reading too fast and skipping words.

function: Ask the child to hold the phone closer and speak clearly.
trigger: Audio quality is too low to score reliably.

function: Check that the child is ready before starting the next item.
trigger: A new item is about to begin after a pause.

function: Ask the child what they think happens next in the story.
trigger: Comprehension check after a story-level item.

function: Repeat the instruction more slowly because the child asked.
trigger: Child said "repeat please" or seemed confused.

function: Tell the child to wait a moment while a facilitator is called.
trigger: The agent needs to hand off to a human facilitator.

function: Ask the child to try a short practice drill before the real item.
trigger: Starting a level-appropriate practice drill.

function: Praise correct letter-sound on the first try.
trigger: Child says the correct sound immediately.

function: Praise correct syllable read on the first try.
trigger: Child reads the syllable correctly immediately.

function: Praise correct word read on the first try.
trigger: Child reads the word correctly immediately.

function: Praise fluent reading of a full paragraph.
trigger: Child reads the paragraph correctly and fluently.

function: Praise finishing a story with strong fluency.
trigger: Child completes a story-level item fluently.

function: Praise the child for succeeding after a retry.
trigger: Child gets a word-level item right on a second attempt.

function: Praise the child for succeeding after a retry at syllable level.
trigger: Child gets a syllable-level item right on a second attempt.

function: Praise a thoughtful answer to a comprehension question.
trigger: Child gives a reasonable answer to a comprehension question.

function: Praise visible effort even when the answer wasn't fully correct.
trigger: Child made a genuine attempt but the item wasn't fully correct.

function: Note that the child is improving compared to earlier in the session.
trigger: Child's accuracy has visibly improved over the session.

function: Praise a confident, clear reading voice.
trigger: Child reads a word-level item clearly and without hesitation.

function: Praise the child for catching and fixing their own mistake.
trigger: Child self-corrects a misread without being prompted.

function: Praise an imaginative answer to an open-ended story question.
trigger: Child gives a creative, on-topic answer to a comprehension question.

function: Gently praise a shy or quiet child's small progress.
trigger: Child is soft-spoken but got a letter/syllable item correct.

function: Prompt the child to think of the sound the letter makes.
trigger: Child pauses more than 3 seconds on a beginner-level item.

function: Prompt the child to blend the two sounds in the syllable together.
trigger: Child hesitates blending a syllable.

function: Prompt the child to look at the first letter of the word.
trigger: Child hesitates on a word-level item.

function: Suggest the word looks like one they already know.
trigger: Child struggles with a word similar to a previously mastered word.

function: Suggest using the rest of the sentence as a clue for the tricky word.
trigger: Child struggles with one word inside a paragraph-level item.

function: Suggest thinking about what would make sense in the story so far.
trigger: Child struggles with a word inside a story-level item.

function: Suggest thinking back to what happened earlier in the story.
trigger: Child struggles to answer a comprehension question.

function: Suggest sounding out the syllable slowly, one part at a time.
trigger: Child misreads a syllable-level item.

function: Suggest looking at the word again carefully before answering.
trigger: Child answers too quickly and gets a word-level item wrong.

function: Suggest breaking the sentence into smaller chunks.
trigger: Child struggles with a long sentence in a paragraph-level item.

function: Suggest thinking of a picture that matches the word.
trigger: Child struggles with a concrete, picturable word.

function: Suggest whispering the sound first before saying it aloud.
trigger: Child seems nervous about saying a beginner-level sound aloud.

function: Gently correct a misread letter sound without saying "wrong".
trigger: Child misreads a beginner-level item.

function: Gently correct a misread syllable.
trigger: Child misreads a syllable-level item.

function: Gently correct a misread word.
trigger: Child misreads a word-level item.

function: Gently correct a misread sentence within a paragraph.
trigger: Child misreads part of a paragraph-level item.

function: Model the correct pronunciation and ask the child to repeat it.
trigger: Child has misread the same word twice.

function: Gently correct a misunderstanding without discouraging the child.
trigger: Child gives an answer that doesn't match the story.

function: Point out gently that a word was skipped and ask them to include it.
trigger: Child skips a word while reading a paragraph-level item.

function: Point out that the sounds came out in the wrong order and ask for another try.
trigger: Child reads a word's sounds out of order.

function: Calmly acknowledge repeated difficulty and offer to move on for now.
trigger: Child has missed the same item three times.

function: Gently correct a mispronounced character or place name in a story.
trigger: Child mispronounces a proper name while reading a story-level item.

function: Announce moving up from beginner to letter/syllable level.
trigger: Child passes the threshold of correct beginner-level items.

function: Announce moving up from letter/syllable to word level.
trigger: Child passes the threshold of correct letter/syllable-level items.

function: Announce moving up from word to paragraph level.
trigger: Child passes the threshold of correct word-level items.

function: Announce moving up from paragraph to story level.
trigger: Child passes the threshold of correct paragraph-level items.

function: Reassure the child they're staying at beginner level to build confidence.
trigger: Child is below the threshold to advance from beginner level.

function: Reassure the child they're staying at letter/syllable level.
trigger: Child is below the threshold to advance from letter/syllable level.

function: Reassure the child they're staying at word level.
trigger: Child is below the threshold to advance from word level.

function: Reassure the child they're staying at paragraph level.
trigger: Child is below the threshold to advance from paragraph level.

function: Gently explain the child will practice letter/syllable items for a bit.
trigger: Assessment shows the child needs to drop back a level.

function: Explain that this first session is about finding the right starting level.
trigger: The very first assessment session for a new child.

function: Encourage a child who seems to be losing focus or getting tired.
trigger: Response latency increases significantly across several items.

function: Reassure a child who seems frustrated after a few misses in a row.
trigger: Child has missed several items in a row.

function: Reassure a shy or nervous-sounding child before they begin.
trigger: Child's voice sounds hesitant at the very start of a session.

function: Encourage the child partway through, noting they're doing this well.
trigger: Session is roughly halfway through its planned items.

function: Encourage the child before a noticeably harder item.
trigger: Next item is meaningfully harder than the last one completed.

function: Welcome the child back warmly after a pause in the session.
trigger: Session resumes after being paused mid-way.

function: Gently ask the child to try speaking a little louder, encouragingly.
trigger: Child's voice is too quiet to score reliably.

function: Gently bring the child's attention back without scolding.
trigger: Background noise or distraction interrupts the session.

function: Close out a normal session and tell the child what happens next.
trigger: Session item queue is complete.

function: Tell the child the session is being paused and can continue later.
trigger: Facilitator or system pauses the session before it's complete.

function: Warmly end a session that's stopping earlier than planned.
trigger: Session ends before the full item queue is finished.

function: Briefly tell the child what level they're working at, in simple terms.
trigger: Session ends and the facilitator wants the child to hear a summary.

function: Thank the child for their effort today, warmly and briefly.
trigger: Session ends, general thank-you moment.

function: Tell the child when or how they'll practice again.
trigger: Session ends and a next session is expected soon.

function: Nothing was heard. Ask the child to try again.
trigger: No speech was detected in the recording.

function: Audio was too quiet. Ask the child to speak a little louder.
trigger: Recorded audio volume is too low to transcribe reliably.

function: Too much background noise. Ask the child to move somewhere quieter or closer to the phone.
trigger: Background noise is too high for reliable transcription.

function: The answer was unclear. Ask the child to say it again.
trigger: Transcript confidence is too low to score the response.

function: The child spoke while the agent was still talking. Ask them to wait for the agent to finish before answering.
trigger: Child's speech overlapped with the agent's own audio playback.

function: Read a low-confidence answer back to the child to confirm it, instead of asking them to redo it.
trigger: Transcript confidence is borderline -- low enough to double check, high enough not to require a full re-record.

function: Alert the facilitator that repeated repair attempts have failed and their attention is needed now.
trigger: Three consecutive repair attempts have failed on the same item.

function: Report a technical fault to the facilitator in plain, factual terms.
trigger: A technical error (recording failure, connectivity loss, crash) prevents the session from continuing normally.

function: Gently acknowledge that the child seems upset and say help is coming right away -- never try to continue the session first.
trigger: Child's speech or behavior signals real distress (crying, panic, refusal). This must always escalate, never be pushed through.

function: Tell the child, simply and reassuringly, that a person is coming to help them now.
trigger: Escalation has been triggered for any reason and the child needs to hear that help is on the way.

function: Ask the facilitator to confirm the assigned reading level before it takes effect.
trigger: The agent has computed a level assignment and it requires facilitator confirmation before being recorded.

function: Report a brief factual summary of the session's results to the facilitator.
trigger: The session has ended and a summary is ready to report.

function: Prompt the facilitator to begin the next child's session.
trigger: The current child's session has ended and another child is waiting.

function: Warn the facilitator that this session's recordings have not yet synced to the server.
trigger: The device has no connectivity and recorded session data is still only stored locally.
